en: Mayon Volcano releases water vapor, a gas, during phreatic eruptions before liquid magma reaches the surface.
Jose Rizal wrote secret letters using invisible ink that required a chemical change to reveal the hidden text.
The Banaue Rice Terraces rely on a heterogeneous mixture of solid soil and liquid water to cultivate rice.
The Philippine Eagle undergoes a physical change when molting solid feathers, replacing them without altering their chemical composition.
The Chocolate Hills consist of solid limestone, a rock that reacts with liquid acid to produce carbon dioxide gas.
Taal Lake contains a homogeneous mixture of dissolved minerals in liquid water, forming a large natural aqueous solution.
The hard shell of the Philippine pili nut contains solid resin that undergoes a chemical change when burned.
Abaca fibers extracted from the Musa textilis plant are solid materials prized for their exceptionally high tensile strength.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features liquid water dripping to form solid stalactites through gradual mineral deposition.
A traditional Philippine jeepney engine burns liquid diesel fuel, converting it into exhaust gases via chemical change.
The carabao cools its body by wallowing in liquid mud, utilizing water's high specific heat capacity.
The famous white sand of Boracay is primarily composed of solid calcium carbonate from crushed coral fragments.
